processing: Fresh buds and leaves from tea plants in Zhaoping County are fixed, rolled, shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Exact picking dates are little documented; as with other Chinese green teas, the spring pickings are normally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Tight, slender, straight strips, silvery green with a hidden jade tone.
appearance_wet: As is typical of tender green tea, even and fresh-looking leaf.
taste_profile: Fresh, smooth and sweet, with a persistent chestnut aroma.

brewing.notes: Usual green tea practice: water off the boil and an open cup, so the chestnut note stays clean rather than stewed.

vintage_note: As usual for Chinese greens, it is sold as the current year's harvest and is best within about a year. The county also makes black tea and Liubao, so check which tea a 'Zhaoping' label actually means.
description:
Zhaoping Cha is the green tea of Zhaoping County in Hezhou, in eastern Guangxi. It holds national geographical indication status, and its calling card is a chestnut aroma.

It is made from tender shoots of local tea plants, which are fixed, rolled, shaped and dried into slim, straight strips with a silvery green look. One local method, known as three firings and three rollings, runs to eight steps.

The liquor is a bright yellow-green and the taste is fresh and sweet, with the chestnut note lingering. It responds to the usual green tea care: water off the boil and no long steeping.

This is a big county industry rather than a small estate tea, with about 250,000 mu of gardens in 2022. Producers also make black tea and Liubao, so read the label and look for the harvest year.
history:
Zhaoping tea had an early mark of recognition in 1988, when the Zhaoping Tea Factory's Green Tea No. 2 was named among Guangxi's six famous teas and won a gold award at the Lu Yu Cup that year.

In 2018 the local tea-making craft was added to Guangxi's intangible cultural heritage list. By 2022 the county counted about 250,000 mu of gardens and about 18,400 tonnes of dry tea.
